title.en: The Spider and the Fly (Mary Howitt)

text.en: Sweet words from a stranger can hide a trap.

A spider invites a fly into his parlour with flattering words. The fly refuses again and again, because she knows that those who go in never come out. At last the spider praises her wings and eyes so much that she is tempted, goes closer and is caught in his web.
The poem is a cautionary tale about flattery. The moral is to beware of people who praise us too much to get what they want. It ends with a warning to young people not to trust flattering words.
Words to learn: parlour, flattery, cunning, winding stair and web. The poem uses a story-like rhyme and a repeated invitation, Will you walk into my parlour.
